rv.q: Yet there are glimmers of brilliance here, from the music to the mental-health drama.
It's undoubtedly a perplexing piece, and while the book could do with a considerable amount of revision, it is deserving of admiration for being so unusual and wilfully uncommercial.
There are moments of genuine tear-jerking emotion that keep Flyby aloft, but this is neither Project Hail Mary nor particularly memorable.
Theo Jamieson's script is meticulously naturalistic, sharply observed, and played adeptly by Gilbert and Thompson
The real tragedy is that it's so clear what the creative team wanted to do, but it never clicks.
Flyby reaches for the stars, yet without a clear trajectory it drifts, and it is only the exceptional cast that stop this journey into the void from feeling entirely weightless.
